title.narrative: The NCD management course provided for 200 chronic NCD patients annually

• # of chronic NCD patients, disaggregated by age, gender, nationality, vulnerability, and Caritas health clinic have been enrolled in and completed a comprehensive NCD management course • At least 75% of chronic NCD patients enrolled in the NCD management course have adopted and are applying healthier dietary and lifestyle changes for improved self-monitoring and daily management of their disease • 40% of the most vulnerable NCD patients have received regular prescribed NCD medication support

target.value: 200 chronic NCD patients have been enrolled in and completed a comprehensive NCD management course At least 75% of chronic NCD patients enrolled in the NCD management course have adopted and are applying healthier dietary and lifestyle changes for improved self-monitoring and daily management of their disease 40% of the most vulnerable NCD patients have received regular prescribed NCD medication support

actual.value: 203 chronic NCD patients (target: 200) (102 F; 83 M) were enrolled in the comprehensive NDC management course of which 197 completed the full year. Of these, 143 were Syrian Refugees (86 F; 57 M) and 60 Jordanian (34 F; 26 M). 86% of NCD patients enrolled in the NCD management course report that the program changed their nutritional behaviour and 89% reported experiencing benefits from the awareness sessions and topics throughout the programme.

title.narrative: Secondary health care services provided to 3,750 of patients annually

• # of patients annually, disaggregated by gender, age and nationality, referred for SHC out-patient diagnostic and treatment services to Caritas partner SHC providers • # of patients annually, disaggregated by gender, age, and nationality, referred for SHC in-patient diagnostic and treatment services (excluding deliveries) to Caritas partner SHC providers • # of women and girls who have delivered in the presence of a skilled attendant under the programme

target.value: 2,490 patients referred to SHC out-patient diagnostic and treatment services annually 285 patients referred to SHC in-patient diagnostic and treatment services annually 36 women and girls who have delivered in the presence of a skilled attendant

actual.value: 3,058 patients (target: 2,810) were referred to and supported with Secondary Health Care (outpatient and inpatient) services at Caritas partner hospitals, laboratories or from specialist consultants. Of these, 2,684 were referred for outpatient care (1,745 F; 936 M and 1,937 Syrian; 744 Jordanian) and 377 for inpatient care (192 F; 185 M and 267 Syrian; 110 Jordanian) of which 28 were deliveries (21 normal vaginal deliveries and 7 caesarean section deliveries).

title.narrative: Primary health care services provided to 6,000 unique patients annually

• # of unique of patients annually, disaggregated by gender, age and nationality, who have received essential primary health care services at Caritas clinics under the programme • # of pregnant women and girls, who have accessed, and utilised maternal and neo-natal health care services provided by Caritas clinics

target.value: 6,000 unique patients receive essential health care services annually 300 pregnant women access, and utilise maternal and neo-natal health care services

actual.value: 6,000 unique patients received PHC services (target: 6,000) including pre- and post-natal monitoring of 300 pregnant women, 6 of whom were <18 years. 89% of the pregnant women attended at least 7 of the 8 standard pre-and post-natal GP check-ups.

title.narrative: CJ actively contributes to coordination of the health sector response in Jordan and efforts to advance and realise the reform of the national health care system

• # of Health Sector Working Group and Sub-group meetings attended and examples of contributions by Caritas Jordan • CJ provides timely input and reporting to JRP and 3RP reporting systems • Examples of Caritas Jordan being recognised as a key partner and contributor within the health sector response to the Syria Crisis in Jordan and the reform of the national health care system

target.value: 10 Health Sector Working Group and Sub-group attended and examples of contributions by Caritas Jordan Timely input and reporting to JRP and 3RP reporting systems Examples of Caritas Jordan being recognised as a key partner and contributor within the health sector response to the Syria Crisis in Jordan and the reform of the national health care system

actual.value: CJ participated in a total of 49 (target: 10) Health Sector and sub-sector Working Group Meetings. Furthermore, CJ participated in a high-level meeting hosted by the Red Crescent on Universal Health Coverage, contributed to a round table discussion on the health sector reform by the German Embassy in Jordan as well as in a meeting hosted by the Danish Embassy in Beirut during a visit to Jordan.

title.narrative: Improved beneficiary, partner and national knowledge, capacity, and coordination to deliver effective health programming and advances in the reform of the national health care system.

• Caritas Jordan has continuously strengthened health staff competencies and programming skills • Caritas Jordan has organisational systems and procedures in place in line with CIMS and CHS • Caritas Jordan collaborates with key health policy actors in their efforts to advance and realize national commitments to health care reform and UHC

target.value:
CJ health clinics operate to national clinical and reporting guidelines. CJ has up-to-date MEAL and PES systems appropriate for the organisation.
More strategic and focussed contribution to national efforts towards an inclusive, less fragmented, national primary healthcare delivery system, primary healthcare reform and development (preventive and curative) more in line with WHO guidelines, and to national efforts and action in support of SDG 3 goals, in particular reduction of NCD premature mortality within the country.
